Result: not reproduced (ed8g-vls-telc-ach-suppressed). The dF/F0 range of the rewarded-trial Ach average is lower in the TelC hemisphere in all 4 mice under both F0 readings (0.013 against 0.019, 0.005 against 0.021, 0.005 against 0.051 and 0.006 against 0.042 under the median F0). The z-scored delta-Ach (reading a) is lower with T1 p < 0.05 in S1142 only under W1 and in three mice under W2, and higher in S952 under both. The criterion requires Ach to be lower "under each reading", and reading (a) fails (S952 higher under W1 and W2, S950 higher under W1, S1143 p = 0.073 under W1). Z-scoring each channel removes the loss of amplitude that TelC causes, as the criterion itself notes, but it still requires reading (a). In S1142 and S1143 the TelC hemisphere is taken as the one carrying virus 222, which the files do not name; the TelC side of S952 is read from the virus names, so the failure does not rest on that assumption. Round 1 recorded reproduced under reading (b); the third verification round agreed with the change to not reproduced.

Result: not reproduced (ed8f-amplitude-no-consistent-effect). The Extended Data Fig. 8 legend gives panel f as "Effect of TelC or mCh expression in CINs on DA release. dF/F0 signals for individual mice ... (n = 4 mice)" and panel g as the simultaneous Ach and DA recordings, so panel f is the dLight1.1 cohort of Fig. 3f. For dLight1.1 the peak dF/F0 is larger in the TelC hemisphere in all 4 mice (+0.008 to +0.030) under both F0 readings, a consistent effect. For rDAh, shown as a variant, the sign is positive in 2 mice and negative in 2. Which cohort the criterion means is asked of a reader (questions/001767.yaml).

ed7e-cin-activation-evokes-da¶

Optogenetic activation of Chrimson-expressing VLS CINs during the task evokes a small, significant DA release, without changing decision or side-port occupancy times.

In [27]:
# ed7e-cin-activation-evokes-da: Chrimson in the left VLS (redL, virus 216), dLight1.1 z-scored in the left hemisphere (greenL);
# stimulated trials = a laser burst starting at side entry (0 or 1 sample); peak z in the 1.5 s from side entry minus the mean
# of the 1.5 s before. The right-hemisphere dLight channel and all raw traces are absent from these files.
CHR = figmice("EDFig12")
rows = []
for s in [s for s in S if s["mouse"] in CHR]:
    L = s["events"]["laser_or_unused"]; starts = L[np.r_[True, np.diff(L) > 10]] if len(L) else L
    t = achda.photometry_trials(s); si = t.photometry_side_in_index.values
    stim = np.isin(si, starts) | np.isin(si + 1, starts)
    n15 = int(round(1.5 / achda.DT))
    z = s["z"]["greenL"]
    post, kp = achda.segments(z, si[:, None] + np.arange(0, n15 + 1)[None, :]); pre, kb = achda.segments(z, si[:, None] + np.arange(-n15, 0)[None, :])
    ok = kp & kb
    post, pre = z[si[ok][:, None] + np.arange(0, n15 + 1)[None, :]], z[si[ok][:, None] + np.arange(-n15, 0)[None, :]]
    change = post.max(1) - pre.mean(1); st = stim[ok]; tt = t[ok]
    occ = (tt.photometry_side_out_index - tt.photometry_side_in_index).values * achda.DT
    dec = (tt.photometry_side_in_index - tt.photometry_center_in_index).values * achda.DT
    rows.append(dict(mouse=s["mouse"], trials=int(ok.sum()), stim_trials=int(st.sum()), change_stim=change[st].mean(), change_nostim=change[~st].mean(),
                     p_T1=achda.t1(change[st], change[~st])[1], occ_stim=occ[st].mean(), occ_nostim=occ[~st].mean(), dec_stim=dec[st].mean(), dec_nostim=dec[~st].mean(),
                     rew_frac_stim=tt.was_rewarded.values[st].mean(), rew_frac_nostim=tt.was_rewarded.values[~st].mean()))
e7 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(e7.round(3).to_string(index=False))
for a, b, lab in (("change_stim", "change_nostim", "peak dLight change"), ("dec_stim", "dec_nostim", "decision time"), ("occ_stim", "occ_nostim", "side-port occupancy")):
    print(f"{lab}: stimulated {e7[a].mean():.3f}, unstimulated {e7[b].mean():.3f}, paired two-sided t-test across {len(e7)} mice p = {stats.ttest_rel(e7[a], e7[b]).pvalue:.4g}")
# rewarded and unrewarded trials separately (a variant)
rows = []
for s in [s for s in S if s["mouse"] in CHR]:
    L = s["events"]["laser_or_unused"]; starts = L[np.r_[True, np.diff(L) > 10]]
    t = achda.photometry_trials(s); si = t.photometry_side_in_index.values; stim = np.isin(si, starts) | np.isin(si + 1, starts)
    n15 = int(round(1.5 / achda.DT)); z = s["z"]["greenL"]
    ok = (si - n15 >= 0) & (si + n15 < len(z))
    ch = z[si[ok][:, None] + np.arange(0, n15 + 1)[None, :]].max(1) - z[si[ok][:, None] + np.arange(-n15, 0)[None, :]].mean(1)
    for rew in (True, False):
        r = t.was_rewarded.values[ok] == rew
        rows.append(dict(mouse=s["mouse"], rewarded=rew, stim=ch[stim[ok] & r].mean(), nostim=ch[~stim[ok] & r].mean()))
v = pd.DataFrame(rows)
for rew, g in v.groupby("rewarded"):
    print(f"{'rewarded' if rew else 'unrewarded'} trials: stimulated {g.stim.mean():.3f}, unstimulated {g.nostim.mean():.3f}, higher when stimulated in {int((g.stim > g.nostim).sum())} of {len(g)} mice, paired p = {stats.ttest_rel(g.stim, g.nostim).pvalue:.4g}")
# Laser artefact and illuminated hemisphere: mean step of each z-scored channel at laser onset (first laser sample minus the one
# before) and offset (first sample after minus the last laser sample), against the s.d. of one-sample steps at random samples.
# A 590-nm laser delivered through a fibre's filter cube shows in that fibre's red channel (Methods, Optogenetic manipulations).
rows = []
for s in [s for s in S if s["mouse"] in CHR]:
    L = s["events"]["laser_or_unused"]; br = np.r_[True, np.diff(L) > 10]; on, off = L[br], L[np.r_[br[1:], True]]
    rnd = np.random.default_rng(int(s["mouse"][1:])).integers(100, s["n_samples"] - 100, 1000)
    row = dict(mouse=s["mouse"], bursts=len(on), burst_samples=f"{(off - on + 1).min()}-{(off - on + 1).max()}")
    for ch in s["z"]:
        z = s["z"][ch]; sd = np.std(z[rnd] - z[rnd - 1])
        row[f"{ch} ({s['meta'][ch]['hemisphere']}, {s['meta'][ch]['sensor']})"] = f"{np.mean(z[on] - z[on - 1]) / sd:+.1f} / {np.mean(z[off + 1] - z[off]) / sd:+.1f}"
    row["greenR z stored"] = "greenR" in s["z"]
    rows.append(row)
print("\nmean step at laser onset / offset, in s.d. of random one-sample steps:"); print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))
# laser-aligned left dLight1.1 against side-entry-aligned unstimulated trials, mean z over the mice
lag = np.arange(-37, 56); A, U = [], []
for s in [s for s in S if s["mouse"] in CHR]:
    L = s["events"]["laser_or_unused"]; on = L[np.r_[True, np.diff(L) > 10]]
    t = achda.photometry_trials(s); si = t.photometry_side_in_index.values; stim = np.isin(si, on) | np.isin(si + 1, on)
    A.append(achda.segments(s["z"]["greenL"], on[:, None] + lag[None, :])[0].mean(0)); U.append(achda.segments(s["z"]["greenL"], si[~stim][:, None] + lag[None, :])[0].mean(0))
A, U = np.mean(A, 0), np.mean(U, 0)
for lo_, hi_ in ((-37, -1), (0, 0), (1, 18), (19, 36), (37, 55)):
    k = (lag >= lo_) & (lag <= hi_)
    print(f"greenL mean z, samples {lo_} to {hi_} from laser onset: {A[k].mean():+.3f}; unstimulated, from side entry: {U[k].mean():+.3f}")

Result: blocked, data missing. In every one of the 7 sessions the laser artefact is in the right fibre: the right red channel (DIO mCherry by the metadata) steps by +2.7 to +5.4 s.d. of one-sample steps at laser onset and -4.5 to -6.4 at offset, while the left channels (dLight1.1 and the Chrimson virus 216) step by at most 0.4. The Methods say only one hemisphere was illuminated in each session, so these sessions illuminated the mCherry hemisphere, whose dLight1.1 trace is not stored. The left dLight1.1 trace, from the hemisphere that was not illuminated, is lower during the laser than after side entry in unstimulated trials (-0.44 against +0.01 z over the 18 samples after onset), and as run the stimulated trials have a smaller peak change than unstimulated ones (1.466 against 1.663 z, lower in 7 of 7 mice, paired p = 5.6e-06). Neither tests CIN activation, and the data do not explain the dip of the left dLight1.1 during the laser. Decision time (1.41 against 1.44 s, p = 0.090) and side-port occupancy (2.10 against 2.10 s, p = 0.997) do not differ with the laser. The bursts last 18 to 20 samples (1.0 s), where the Methods give 1.5 s.

fig4g-cko-ach-suppression-lost and fig4g-cko-da-unchanged¶

fig4g-ach: In Drd2-cKO mice the two dips in Ach that coincide with DA rises are lost, so Ach signals are significantly larger than in Drd2 f/f and wild-type mice.

fig4g-da: DA dynamics during the task do not differ significantly across WT, Drd2 f/f and Drd2-cKO mice.

# fig4g-cko-ach-suppression-lost and fig4g-cko-da-unchanged: windows of aa_processStats_final_Fig4_cKO_Ach_Words.m
# (post +1..+18 and +9..+16; all trials, pre -18..-1 and -18..-9 samples about side entry); Ach3.0 = greenL, rDAh = redL
WIN4 = {"post +1..+18": np.arange(1, 19), "post +9..+16": np.arange(9, 17), "pre -18..-1": np.arange(-18, 0), "pre -18..-9": np.arange(-18, -8)}
f4keys = set(zip(uses[uses.Figure == "Fig4"].Mouse, uses[uses.Figure == "Fig4"].date))
GENO = {m: g for g in ("wt", "ff", "cko") for m in GROUPS[g]}
rows = []
for s in S:
    if s["mouse"] not in GENO or (s["mouse"], s["date"]) not in f4keys:
        continue
    t = achda.photometry_trials(s)
    for sig, ch, meas in (("Ach", "greenL", "range"), ("DA", "redL", "mean"), ("Ach mean (variant)", "greenL", "mean")):
        if ch not in s["z"]:
            continue
        for wn, off in WIN4.items():
            seg, keep = achda.segments(s["z"][ch], t.photometry_side_in_index.values[:, None] + off[None, :])
            rows.append(pd.DataFrame({"mouse": s["mouse"], "geno": GENO[s["mouse"]], "signal": sig, "window": wn, "rew": t.was_rewarded.values[keep], "v": achda.measure(seg, meas)}))
G4 = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)
chk = pd.Series([(s["meta"].get("redL", {}).get("sensor"), s["meta"].get("greenL", {}).get("sensor"), "redL" in s["z"], "greenL" in s["z"])
                 for s in S if s["mouse"] in GENO and (s["mouse"], s["date"]) in f4keys])
print("Drd2 cohort sessions by (redL sensor, greenL sensor, redL z stored, greenL z stored):", chk.value_counts().to_dict())
print("mice per genotype with each signal:", G4.groupby(["signal", "geno"]).mouse.nunique().to_dict())
res = []
for (sig, wn), g in G4.groupby(["signal", "window"]):
    for tt, d in (("all", g), ("rewarded", g[g.rew]), ("unrewarded", g[~g.rew])):
        if wn.startswith("pre") and tt != "all":
            continue
        for unit in ("(a) mouse means", "(b) trials pooled"):
            dd = d.groupby(["geno", "mouse"]).v.mean().reset_index() if unit.startswith("(a)") else d
            v = {k: dd[dd.geno == k].v.values for k in ("wt", "ff", "cko")}
            res.append(dict(signal=sig, window=wn, trials=tt, unit=unit, mean_wt=v["wt"].mean(), mean_ff=v["ff"].mean(), mean_cko=v["cko"].mean(),
                            anova_p=stats.f_oneway(v["wt"], v["ff"], v["cko"]).pvalue, p_cko_vs_ff=stats.ttest_ind(v["cko"], v["ff"]).pvalue,
                            p_cko_vs_wt=stats.ttest_ind(v["cko"], v["wt"]).pvalue))
F4 = pd.DataFrame(res)
print(F4[F4.signal == "Ach"].round(5).to_string(index=False))
print(); print(F4[F4.signal == "DA"].round(5).to_string(index=False))

Result: not reproduced (fig4g-cko-ach-suppression-lost). With one value per mouse (reading a) the ANOVA of delta-Ach across genotypes is not significant in any window (p = 0.73 before side entry, 0.89 and 0.98 after it in rewarded trials). With trials pooled (reading b) every ANOVA gives p < 1e-5, but Drd2-cKO delta-Ach is below WT before side entry (2.98 against 3.10) and in the rewarded +9 to +16 window (2.10 against 2.15). The mean z-scored Ach, a variant (the paper's code computes both measures and the Extended Data Fig. 11d legend does not say which it plots), does separate the genotypes with one value per mouse: before side entry (-18 to -1) ANOVA p = 0.0005, Drd2-cKO above Drd2 f/f (p = 0.003) and WT (p = 0.001); after side entry in rewarded trials (+9 to +16) p = 0.0001, cKO above both (p = 0.003 and 0.00006).

Result: not reproduced (fig4g-cko-da-unchanged). Under reading (a) the ANOVA of mean rDAh is significant in the +9 to +16 window over all trials (p = 0.039; Drd2-cKO 0.39 against 0.26 and 0.22 z) and in rewarded trials (p = 0.049); the other windows give p ≥ 0.11.

fig5b-glutamate-not-lateralized, fig5c-glutamate-like-ach and fig5d-terminal-calcium-coincides¶

fig5b: Striatal glutamate varies during the task and does not differ between ipsiversive and contraversive trials.

fig5c: Glutamate is suppressed before the choice and rises at side-port entry like Ach, and in rewarded trials shows a sustained rise during consumption that is absent in unrewarded trials.

fig5d: Calcium activity in cortical and thalamic terminals in the VLS coincides with glutamate release in rewarded and unrewarded trials.

In [29]:
# Fig. 5 cohorts: glutamate (iGluSnFR, labelled "glutamate sensor"), S1299-S1302; Ach3.0 with jRCaMP1b (thalamic terminals), the
# Fig5 WT mice with a jRcamp1b channel; retrograde GCaMP8 (cortical terminals), WT74-WT79
GLU = figmice("Fig5", "Chat Jax")
JRC = sorted({s["mouse"] for s in S if s["mouse"] in figmice("Fig5", "WT C57") and any(s["meta"][c]["sensor"] == "jRcamp1b" for c in s["meta"])})
GC8 = sorted({s["mouse"] for s in S if any("Gcamp8" in s["meta"][c]["sensor"] for c in s["meta"])})
f5 = sessions_of(GLU + JRC + GC8, "Fig5")
def chan_with(s, test):
    return [c for c in achda.CHANNELS if c in s["z"] and test(s["meta"][c]["sensor"])]
print("glutamate mice", GLU, "; jRCaMP1b mice", JRC, "; GCaMP8 mice", GC8)
print("sessions with each stream:", {lab: sum(bool(chan_with(s, f)) for s in f5) for lab, f in (("glutamate", lambda x: x == "glutamate sensor"), ("Ach3.0", lambda x: x == "Ach3.0"), ("jRcamp1b", lambda x: x == "jRcamp1b"), ("GCaMP8", lambda x: "Gcamp8" in x))})
# fig5b-glutamate-not-lateralized
rows = []
for s in [s for s in f5 if s["mouse"] in GLU]:
    t = achda.photometry_trials(s)
    for ch in chan_with(s, lambda x: x == "glutamate sensor"):
        ipsi = np.where(s["meta"][ch]["hemisphere"] == "left", t.chose_left.values, ~t.chose_left.values)
        for rd in ("W1", "W2"):
            for which in ("pre", "post"):
                seg, keep = achda.segments(s["z"][ch], achda.window_idx(t.photometry_side_in_index.values, which, rd))
                rows.append(pd.DataFrame({"mouse": s["mouse"], "chan": ch, "reading": rd, "which": which, "ipsi": ipsi[keep], "v": seg.mean(1)}))
G5 = pd.concat(rows)
out = []
for (ch, rd, which, m), g in G5.groupby(["chan", "reading", "which", "mouse"]):
    e, p = achda.t1(g[g.ipsi].v, g[~g.ipsi].v); out.append(dict(chan=ch, reading=rd, window=which, mouse=m, ipsi_minus_contra=e, p=p))
out = pd.DataFrame(out)
print("\nfig5b, glutamate ipsilateral minus contralateral, T1 per mouse:"); print(out.pivot_table(index=["chan", "reading", "window"], columns="mouse", values=["ipsi_minus_contra", "p"]).round(4).to_string())
print(out.groupby(["chan", "reading", "window"]).p.apply(lambda p: int((p < 0.05).sum())).rename("mice with p < 0.05").to_string())
# trial-averaged traces about side entry (-2 to +3 s) and centre entry, per mouse
SPAN = np.arange(int(round(-2 / achda.DT)), int(round(3 / achda.DT)) + 1)
def mouse_trace(mice, test, rew=None, align="side"):
    out = {}
    for m in mice:
        segs = []
        for s in [s for s in f5 if s["mouse"] == m]:
            chs = chan_with(s, test)
            if not chs:
                continue
            t = achda.photometry_trials(s)
            if rew is not None:
                t = t[t.was_rewarded == rew]
            ev = (t.photometry_side_in_index if align == "side" else t.photometry_center_in_index).values
            seg, _ = achda.segments(s["z"][chs[0]], ev[:, None] + SPAN[None, :]); segs.append(seg)
        if segs:
            out[m] = np.vstack(segs).mean(0)
    return out
is_glu, is_ach, is_jrc, is_gc8 = (lambda x: x == "glutamate sensor"), (lambda x: x == "Ach3.0"), (lambda x: x == "jRcamp1b"), (lambda x: "Gcamp8" in x)
tsec = SPAN * achda.DT; z0 = int(np.flatnonzero(SPAN == 0)[0])
glu = mouse_trace(GLU, is_glu); glu_c = mouse_trace(GLU, is_glu, align="center"); ach = mouse_trace(JRC, is_ach)
gm, gcm, am = np.mean(list(glu.values()), 0), np.mean(list(glu_c.values()), 0), np.mean(list(ach.values()), 0)
pre_w1 = gm[z0 - 17:z0].mean()
sel = (tsec >= -1) & (tsec <= 1)
rise = gm[z0:z0 + 10].max() - gm[z0]
print(f"\nfig5c: {len(glu)} glutamate mice, {len(ach)} Ach mice. Mean glutamate in the pre window (W1) {pre_w1:.3f} against its value at centre entry {gcm[z0]:.3f}; "
      f"rise within 0.5 s of side entry (max minus value at entry) {rise:.3f}; r(glutamate, Ach) from -1 to +1 s = {np.corrcoef(gm[sel], am[sel])[0, 1]:.3f}")
rows = []
for m in GLU:
    v = {}
    for rew in (True, False):
        segs = []
        for s in [s for s in f5 if s["mouse"] == m]:
            t = achda.photometry_trials(s); t = t[t.was_rewarded == rew]
            seg, _ = achda.segments(s["z"][chan_with(s, is_glu)[0]], t.photometry_side_in_index.values[:, None] + np.arange(int(1 / achda.DT), int(3 / achda.DT) + 1)[None, :]); segs.append(seg.mean(1))
        v[rew] = np.concatenate(segs)
    e, p = achda.t1(v[True], v[False]); rows.append(dict(mouse=m, rewarded=v[True].mean(), unrewarded=v[False].mean(), diff=e, p=p))
print("glutamate 1-3 s after side entry, rewarded against unrewarded:"); print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(4).to_string(index=False))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3)); ax.plot(tsec, gm, label="glutamate"); ax.plot(tsec, am, label="Ach"); ax.axvline(0, ls=":"); ax.legend(); ax.set_xlabel("s from side entry"); plt.show()
print("plotted ranges: glutamate %.2f to %.2f, Ach %.2f to %.2f" % (gm.min(), gm.max(), am.min(), am.max()))
# fig5d-terminal-calcium-coincides
for rew in (True, False):
    g = np.mean(list(mouse_trace(GLU, is_glu, rew).values()), 0)
    for lab, mice, test in (("jRCaMP1b, thalamic", JRC, is_jrc), ("GCaMP8, cortical", GC8, is_gc8)):
        tr = mouse_trace(mice, test, rew)
        c = np.mean(list(tr.values()), 0)
        print(f"fig5d, {'rewarded' if rew else 'unrewarded'}, {lab}: {len(tr)} mice, r(mean calcium, mean glutamate) over -2..+3 s = {np.corrcoef(c, g)[0, 1]:.3f}; "
              f"per mouse r = {[round(np.corrcoef(v, g)[0, 1], 2) for v in tr.values()]}")

Result: not reproduced (fig5b-glutamate-not-lateralized). After side entry glutamate differs between ipsilateral and contralateral trials in 4 of 4 mice on the left fibre (W1 and W2, +0.09 to +0.43 z) and 3 of 4 on the right; before side entry 2 or 3 of 4.

Result: partially reproduced (fig5c-glutamate-like-ach). Glutamate rises within 0.5 s of side entry (by 0.229 z), its mean trace correlates with the Ach trace of the 9 jRCaMP1b mice from -1 to +1 s (r = 0.410), and from 1 to 3 s after side entry it is higher in rewarded than unrewarded trials in 4 of 4 mice (by 0.53 to 0.83 z, p < 0.0001). Before side entry it is not below its value at centre entry (-0.335 against -0.362 z).

Result: reproduced (fig5d-terminal-calcium-coincides). The mean jRCaMP1b trace (thalamic terminals, 9 mice where the paper has 6) correlates with the mean glutamate trace at r = 0.849 (rewarded) and 0.676 (unrewarded), and the GCaMP8 trace (cortical terminals, 5 mice) at 0.912 and 0.790.

fig5ef-input-telc-dampens-ach and fig5ef-input-specific-ach¶

fig5ef-dampens: Silencing cortical or thalamic glutamatergic inputs with TelC robustly lowers Ach sensor dF/F0 across all trials, consistently across mice.

fig5ef-specific: In unrewarded trials, loss of cortical but not thalamic input perturbs Ach after side-port entry, and loss of thalamic input shifts the timing of Ach transients more than loss of cortical input.

In [30]:
# fig5ef: Ach3.0 (greenL) in cortical (Vglut1-Cre) and thalamic (Vglut2-Cre) TelC and mCherry mice
INP = {"cortex": ("ctx_TelC", "ctx_mCh"), "thalamus": ("thal_TelC", "thal_mCh")}
rows = []
for inp, (gt, gm_) in INP.items():
    for grp in (gt, gm_):
        for m in GROUPS[grp]:
            for s in [s for s in S if s["mouse"] == m]:
                ch = "greenL"
                row = dict(input=inp, group="TelC" if grp == gt else "mCherry", mouse=m, has_z=ch in s["z"], has_raw=ch in s["raw"])
                t = achda.photometry_trials(s)
                if ch in s["raw"]:
                    for f0 in ("median", "rolling"):
                        row[f"range_dff_{f0}"] = dff_range(s, ch, f0, rew=None)[0]
                if ch in s["z"]:
                    tn = t[~t.was_rewarded]
                    for rd in ("W1", "W2"):
                        seg, _ = achda.segments(s["z"][ch], achda.window_idx(tn.photometry_side_in_index.values, "post", rd))
                        row[f"dAch_{rd}"] = (seg.max(1) - seg.min(1)).mean()
                    seg, _ = achda.segments(s["z"][ch], tn.photometry_side_in_index.values[:, None] + np.arange(0, int(2 / achda.DT) + 1)[None, :])
                    row["peak_latency_s"] = seg.mean(0).argmax() * achda.DT
                rows.append(row)
E5 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
# channel metadata and the export table's virus codes of each input group (also the groups of ed13-input-telc-behaviour)
for grp in ("ctx_TelC", "ctx_mCh", "thal_TelC", "thal_mCh"):
    for m in GROUPS[grp]:
        meta = sorted({(c, s["meta"][c]["sensor"], s["meta"][c]["brainRegion"], s["meta"][c]["hemisphere"], s["meta"][c]["virus"]) for s in S if s["mouse"] == m for c in s["meta"]})
        row = csv[csv.Mouse == m].iloc[0]
        print(grp, m, row.Genotype, "| table virus codes ch1/ch2/ch5/ch6:", [row[c] for c in ("Ch1_Virus", "Ch2_Virus", "Ch5_Virus", "Ch6_Virus")], "| files:", meta)
print(E5.round(4).to_string(index=False))
for inp in INP:
    d = E5[E5.input == inp]
    for col in [c for c in ("range_dff_median", "range_dff_rolling") if c in d]:
        a, b = d[d.group == "TelC"][col].dropna(), d[d.group == "mCherry"][col].dropna()
        print(f"fig5ef dampens, {inp}, {col}: TelC {list(a.round(4))}, mCherry {list(b.round(4))}; every TelC below the smallest mCherry: "
              f"{bool(len(a) and len(b) and (a < b.min()).all()) if len(b) else 'no mCherry raw traces'}")

        print(f"fig5ef specific, {inp}, unrewarded delta-Ach {rd}: TelC {a.mean():.3f}, mCherry {b.mean():.3f}, two-sample t-test p = {stats.ttest_ind(a, b).pvalue:.4f}")
    lat = d.groupby("group").peak_latency_s.mean()
    print(f"  {inp}: mean latency of the unrewarded Ach peak, TelC {lat['TelC']:.3f} s, mCherry {lat['mCherry']:.3f} s, shift {abs(lat['TelC'] - lat['mCherry']):.3f} s")

Result: partially reproduced (fig5ef-input-telc-dampens-ach). For the cortex the dF/F0 range of every TelC mouse (0.011 to 0.016) is below the smallest mCherry range (0.022) under both F0 readings, for the 3 of the paper's 5 TelC mice that the dataset holds. For the thalamus the three mCherry mice have no raw trace in the files, so their dF/F0 cannot be formed and the thalamic half is not tested. The thalamic mCherry mice (S1351, S1389, S1393, Vglut2-Cre) carry virus 349, named retro mCherry and given as in the VLS, in both hemispheres, the virus and region of the cortical mCherry mice; the thalamic TelC mice carry 336 (SIO-tetanus mCh) in the left VLS. The Fig. 5f legend describes "TelC or mCh expression in the thalamus", and the Results say TelC was injected directly into the thalamus. The files do not record an injection into the thalamus for either group, so whether the thalamic controls received a thalamic injection cannot be checked.

Result: not reproduced (fig5ef-input-specific-ach). Unrewarded delta-Ach does not differ between cortical TelC and mCherry mice (p = 0.40 under W1, 0.26 under W2), and the peak latency shifts less for thalamic (0.108 s) than for cortical TelC (0.162 s).

ed2op-mutant-sensors-flat¶

The DA and Ach transients depend on neuromodulator binding, being absent with the ligand-binding-site mutant sensors.

GLMs: ed5-base-glm-r2, ed5f-leave-out and ed5-history-glm-r2¶

ed5-base: A base GLM of behavioural events explains about a fifth of the variance of trial-associated DA and Ach signals (test R2 0.206 for each).

ed5f: Leaving out side entry or reward raises the GLM's MSE for both DA and Ach, leaving out side exit or lick raises it for Ach, and leaving out centre entry or centre exit alone does not change it.

ed5-history: Adding side entries split by the eight action-outcome histories improves the GLM, to a test R2 of 0.213 for DA and 0.214 for Ach, with a lower MSE and no overfitting.

The cohort is the export table's EDFig10 sessions; the GLM code is not published, so the predictor set (P1, P2), the pooling (G1 to G3) and Y are run as the claims file names them.

In [32]:
# GLMs (Methods, GLM): OLS on trial segments, 41 shifts per predictor, 50/50 trial split per run, test R2 averaged over runs.
# Pooling readings: G1 one model over all sessions of all mice, G2 one per mouse, G3 one per session (R2 averaged).
P1_NAMES = ["centre_entry", "centre_exit", "side_entry", "side_exit", "lick", "reward"]
def glm_units(cohort, predictor_set, history, continuous=None):
    units = []
    for s, ch_y, mouse in cohort:
        cont = {k: s["z"][c].astype(float) for k, c in (continuous(s) if continuous else {}).items()}
        X, y, trial_of, names = achda.glm_session(s, ch_y, achda.glm_events(s, predictor_set, history), cont)
        units.append(dict(mouse=mouse, session=s["date"], X=X, y=y, trial=trial_of, names=names))
    return units

def make_splits(units, runs, rng):
    """Test trials (half of each unit's trials) for each run, shared by every model fitted to the same units, so that their
    test MSE can be compared run by run."""
    return [[rng.choice(np.unique(u["trial"]), len(np.unique(u["trial"])) // 2, replace=False) for u in units] for _ in range(runs)]

def run_glm(units, splits, rng, leave_out=None, folds=0):
    """Test R2, train R2, test MSE and kernels (mean over the reading's models) per run and pooling reading."""
    names = units[0]["names"]
    out = {k: {g: [] for g in ("G1", "G2", "G3")} for k in ("r2", "train_r2", "mse", "kernels")}; val = []
    for r, tests in enumerate(splits):
        tr_st, te_st, fold_st = [], [], []
        for u, test in zip(units, tests):
            trials = np.unique(u["trial"])
            te = np.isin(u["trial"], test)
            tr_st.append(achda.suff_stats(u["X"], u["y"], ~te)); te_st.append(achda.suff_stats(u["X"], u["y"], te))
            if folds:
                train_trials = np.setdiff1d(trials, test); fs = []
                for f in range(folds):
                    v = rng.choice(train_trials, int(round(0.2 * len(train_trials))), replace=False)
                    fs.append(achda.suff_stats(u["X"], u["y"], np.isin(u["trial"], v)))
                fold_st.append(fs)
        groups = {"G1": [list(range(len(units)))],
                  "G2": [[i for i, u in enumerate(units) if u["mouse"] == m] for m in sorted({u["mouse"] for u in units})],
                  "G3": [[i] for i in range(len(units))]}
        for g, parts in groups.items():
            vals, trv, ms, ks = [], [], [], []
            for idx in parts:
                trs = tr_st[idx[0]]; tes = te_st[idx[0]]
                for i in idx[1:]:
                    trs = achda.add_stats(trs, tr_st[i]); tes = achda.add_stats(tes, te_st[i])
                b = achda.fit_ols(trs)
                vals.append(achda.r2(tes, b)); trv.append(achda.r2(trs, b)); ms.append(achda.sse(tes, b) / tes["n"]); ks.append(b)
                if folds:
                    models = {"full": None, **{f"-{p}": [j for j, n in enumerate(names) if not n.startswith(p + ":")] for p in leave_out}}
                    for mname, cols in models.items():
                        tot_sse, tot_n = 0.0, 0
                        for f in range(folds):
                            vs = fold_st[idx[0]][f]
                            for i in idx[1:]:
                                vs = achda.add_stats(vs, fold_st[i][f])
                            bf = achda.fit_ols(achda.add_stats(trs, vs, -1), cols)
                            tot_sse += achda.sse(vs, bf, cols); tot_n += vs["n"]
                        val.append(dict(run=r, reading=g, unit=len(vals) - 1, model=mname, val_mse=tot_sse / tot_n))
            for k, v in (("r2", vals), ("train_r2", trv), ("mse", ms)):
                out[k][g].append(float(np.mean(v)))
            out["kernels"][g].append(np.mean(ks, 0))
    res = {k: {g: np.array(v) for g, v in d.items()} for k, d in out.items()}
    res["names"] = names; res["val"] = pd.DataFrame(val)
    return res

def glm_table(results, label):
    rows = []
    for key, res in results.items():
        sig, pset = key[0], key[-1]
        for g, v in res["r2"].items():
            rows.append(dict(model=label, signal=sig, **({"group": key[1]} if len(key) == 3 else {}), predictors=pset, pooling=g, R2_Y10=v.mean(), R2_Y3=v[:3].mean(),
                             R2_min=v.min(), R2_max=v.max(), train_R2=res["train_r2"][g].mean(), test_MSE=res["mse"][g].mean()))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def kernel(res, pooling, prefix):
    """Coefficients of one predictor over the 41 shifts (rows: runs), and the shifts. In the history GLMs the side entries of
    the four rewarded histories sum to the reward predictor (reward is coded at the side entry of rewarded trials), so their
    kernels are not identified apart from it; for those the identified sum, history kernel plus reward kernel, is returned."""
    def cols_of(p):
        return [j for j, n in enumerate(res["names"]) if n.split(":")[0] == p]
    cols = cols_of(prefix)
    K = res["kernels"][pooling][:, cols]
    if prefix.startswith("side_entry_") and prefix[-1].isupper():
        K = K + res["kernels"][pooling][:, cols_of("reward")]
    return K, np.array([int(res["names"][j].split(":")[1]) for j in cols])

# Extended Data Fig. 5 cohort: the CSV's EDFig10 sessions (the GLM figure of the export table; the published figure is Extended Data Fig. 5).
# DA: dLight1.1 where the mouse has it (greenR, else greenL), otherwise rDAh (redL); Ach: Ach3.0 (greenL).
e5 = sessions_of(figmice("EDFig10"), "EDFig10")
def da_chan(s):
    for c in ("greenR", "greenL"):
        if c in s["z"] and s["meta"][c]["sensor"] == "dlight1.1":
            return c
    return "redL" if "redL" in s["z"] and s["meta"]["redL"]["sensor"] == "rDAh" else None
COH5 = {"DA": [(s, da_chan(s), s["mouse"]) for s in e5 if da_chan(s)],
        "Ach": [(s, "greenL", s["mouse"]) for s in e5 if "greenL" in s["z"] and s["meta"]["greenL"]["sensor"] == "Ach3.0"]}
for k, v in COH5.items():
    print(f"{k}: {len({m for _, _, m in v})} mice, {len(v)} sessions; channels {pd.Series([c for _, c, _ in v]).value_counts().to_dict()}")

        ub = glm_units(COH5[sig], pset, False)

        BASE[(sig, pset)] = run_glm(ub, splits, rng, leave_out=P1_NAMES, folds=10)
        HIST[(sig, pset)] = run_glm(glm_units(COH5[sig], pset, True), splits, rng)

g5 = pd.concat([glm_table(BASE, "base"), glm_table(HIST, "history")])

Result: blocked, methods underspecified (ed5-base-glm-r2). The tolerance is 0.185 to 0.227. One model per mouse (G2) puts both R2 inside it (DA 0.203 with P1 and 0.212 with P2; Ach 0.216 and 0.227), and one per session (G3) puts DA inside (0.211, 0.216) but Ach above (0.244, 0.249); one model over all sessions (G1) gives 0.132 and 0.138 for DA and 0.159 and 0.167 for Ach. Y = 3 and Y = 10 agree to 0.002. The readings disagree, which the criterion says blocks the claim.

Result: partially reproduced (ed5f-leave-out). The criterion fails under every reading, so the open GLM readings do not change the outcome. Leaving out reward raises the DA validation MSE beyond the full model's range under all 6 DA readings (P1 and P2 by G1 to G3; rise 0.021 to 0.030), but leaving out side entry does not under any (rise 0.003 to 0.008). For Ach, leaving out side entry raises it beyond the range with P1 only, reward under 5 of 6 readings, lick under G1 and G3 with P1, and side exit under none (rise 0.008 to 0.012). Leaving out centre entry or centre exit keeps the median within the full model's range in 11 of the 12 signal-reading pairs; with P2 and G3 the DA median without centre entry falls just below it (0.7631 against a minimum of 0.7632). The criterion fixes Y = 10 runs. With the first 3 runs, shown as a variant, the narrower range of 3 runs lets more rises clear it, but no reading has every part hold for both signals (DA only with P2 and G2, Ach only with P1 and G3).

Result: blocked, methods underspecified (ed5-history-glm-r2). The history model's test MSE is below the base model's in 10 of 10 runs under every reading, on the same test trials. Its R2 is within tolerance under G2 and G3 for DA (0.214 to 0.223) and under G2 with P1 for Ach (0.231), and outside it otherwise (DA G1 0.146 and 0.150; Ach G1 0.181 and 0.188, G2 with P2 0.240, G3 0.253 and 0.257), so the readings disagree. Train and test R2 are equal under G1, and the train R2 exceeds the test R2 by 0.014 to 0.032 under G2 and by 0.06 to 0.08 under G3, one model per session overfitting most.

fig2h-photometry-glm¶

Kernels of a GLM that predicts one neuromodulator from the other show a negative interaction at about 100 ms; photometry alone predicts weakly (R2 0.116 for DA, 0.171 for Ach), and adding the photometry kernels to the history GLMs raises R2 to 0.336 for DA and 0.388 for Ach.

Run under the pooling and predictor readings of ed5-base-glm-r2; the criterion asks for every reading.

In [35]:
# fig2h-photometry-glm: the 6 Fig2 mice, rDAh (redL) and Ach3.0 (greenL) in the left hemisphere. The other channel's z-scored
# signal is a continuous predictor with the same 41 shifts; a column for shift k at sample n holds the predictor at n - k, so a
# positive shift means the predicted signal follows the predictor. The legend's kernels are from the GLM "that incorporates
# behavioural, history and photometry variables" (Fig. 2h legend); those of the photometry-only GLM are shown as well.
t0 = time.time()
rng = np.random.default_rng(2008)
COH2 = [(s, None, s["mouse"]) for s in f2 if "redL" in s["z"] and "greenL" in s["z"]
        and s["meta"]["redL"]["sensor"] == "rDAh" and s["meta"]["greenL"]["sensor"] == "Ach3.0"]
print(f"{len({m for _, _, m in COH2})} mice, {len(COH2)} sessions")
other = {"DA": ("redL", "greenL", "ach"), "Ach": ("greenL", "redL", "da")}
PH = {}
for sig, (ch_y, ch_x, xname) in other.items():
    coh = [(s, ch_y, m) for s, _, m in COH2]
    only = glm_units(coh, "P1", False, continuous=lambda s, c=ch_x, n=xname: {n: c})
    for u in only:                                    # photometry only: intercept and the 41 shifts of the other signal
        keep = [j for j, n in enumerate(u["names"]) if n == "intercept" or n.startswith(xname + ":")]
        u["X"] = u["X"][:, keep]; u["names"] = [u["names"][j] for j in keep]
    splits = make_splits(only, 10, rng)
    PH[(sig, "photometry only", "-")] = run_glm(only, splits, rng)
    for pset in ("P1", "P2"):
        PH[(sig, "history + photometry", pset)] = run_glm(glm_units(coh, pset, True, continuous=lambda s, c=ch_x, n=xname: {n: c}), splits, rng)
print(f"GLMs fitted in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
rows = []
for (sig, model, pset), res in PH.items():
    xname = other[sig][2]
    for g in ("G1", "G2", "G3"):
        K, shifts = kernel(res, g, xname)
        mk = K.mean(0); i = mk.argmin()
        rows.append(dict(signal=sig, model=model, predictors=pset, pooling=g, R2=res["r2"][g].mean(), R2_Y3=res["r2"][g][:3].mean(), R2_min=res["r2"][g].min(), R2_max=res["r2"][g].max(),
                         kernel_min=mk[i], kernel_min_shift=int(shifts[i]), kernel_min_ms=round(shifts[i] * 1000 * achda.DT),
                         kernel_max=mk.max(), kernel_max_shift=int(shifts[mk.argmax()]), shift_in_54_162ms=bool(1 <= shifts[i] <= 3)))
fig2h = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Tolerances: DA from Ach only 0.104-0.128; Ach from DA only 0.154-0.188; DA history + photometry 0.302-0.370; Ach 0.349-0.427")
print(fig2h.round(4).to_string(index=False))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3))
for a, sig in zip(ax, ("Ach", "DA")):
    K, shifts = kernel(PH[(sig, "history + photometry", "P1")], "G2", other[sig][2])
    a.plot(shifts * achda.DT, K.mean(0)); a.fill_between(shifts * achda.DT, K.mean(0) - K.std(0), K.mean(0) + K.std(0), alpha=0.3)
    a.axvline(0, ls=":"); a.set_title(f"{other[sig][2]} kernel predicting {sig} (P1, G2)"); a.set_xlabel("shift (s), predictor earlier > 0")
    print(f"{sig}: plotted kernel range {K.mean(0).min():.4f} to {K.mean(0).max():.4f}")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

Result: not reproduced. On the 6 mice (29 sessions), the photometry-only GLMs give test R2 of 0.072, 0.094 and 0.109 for DA from Ach (G1, G2, G3; tolerance 0.104 to 0.128, only G3 inside) and 0.098, 0.118 and 0.136 for Ach from DA (tolerance 0.154 to 0.188, all below). The history GLMs with photometry give 0.166 to 0.270 for DA (tolerance 0.302 to 0.370, all below) and 0.268 to 0.366 for Ach (0.349 to 0.427, inside under G2 and G3). The criterion fails under every reading, and Y = 3 gives the same R2 to within 0.001. The DA kernel that predicts Ach has its most negative coefficient at +1 sample (54 ms, Ach following DA) in every model and reading, -0.098 to -0.117. The Ach kernel that predicts DA has its minimum at -1 sample, so there the predicted DA precedes the predictor, as the DA-leads-Ach lag of fig2d implies. The criterion asks that the predicted signal follow the predictor in both models, which that lag rules out for DA predicted from Ach; this is asked of a reader (questions/001767.yaml). It does not change the outcome, as the R2 part fails.

ed11-cko-glm-r2¶

History GLMs fit DA and Ach signals of the three genotypes with test R2 of 0.129, 0.122 and 0.155 for DA and 0.202, 0.262 and 0.214 for Ach (WT, Drd2 f/f, Drd2-cKO); side-entry Ach kernels are greatly altered in Drd2-cKO mice while DA kernels are comparable.

In [36]:
# ed11-cko-glm-r2: history GLM per genotype (Drd2 cohort, Fig4 sessions), rDAh (redL) and Ach3.0 (greenL). Side-entry kernels
# for each of the eight histories; bands are the mean +/- s.d. over the 10 runs of the reading's kernel.
t0 = time.time()
rng = np.random.default_rng(2011)
H11 = {}
for sig, ch, sensor in (("DA", "redL", "rDAh"), ("Ach", "greenL", "Ach3.0")):
    for g in ("wt", "ff", "cko"):
        coh = [(s, ch, s["mouse"]) for s in S if s["mouse"] in GROUPS[g] and (s["mouse"], s["date"]) in f4keys
               and ch in s["z"] and s["meta"][ch]["sensor"] == sensor]
        splits = None
        for pset in ("P1", "P2"):
            u = glm_units(coh, pset, True)
            splits = splits or make_splits(u, 10, rng)
            H11[(sig, g, pset)] = run_glm(u, splits, rng)
print(f"GLMs fitted in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
t11 = glm_table(H11, "history")
t11["n_mice"] = [len({u for u in GROUPS[g]}) for g in t11.group]
TOL11 = {("DA", "wt"): 0.129, ("DA", "ff"): 0.122, ("DA", "cko"): 0.155, ("Ach", "wt"): 0.202, ("Ach", "ff"): 0.262, ("Ach", "cko"): 0.214}
t11["paper"] = [TOL11[(s, g)] for s, g in zip(t11.signal, t11.group)]
t11["within_10pct"] = (t11.R2_Y10 - t11.paper).abs() <= 0.1 * t11.paper
t11["within_10pct_Y3"] = (t11.R2_Y3 - t11.paper).abs() <= 0.1 * t11.paper
print(t11[["signal", "group", "predictors", "pooling", "R2_Y10", "R2_Y3", "R2_min", "R2_max", "paper", "within_10pct", "within_10pct_Y3"]].round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("mice per genotype and signal:", {(sig, g): len({s["mouse"] for s in S if s["mouse"] in GROUPS[g] and (s["mouse"], s["date"]) in f4keys
                                        and ch in s["z"] and s["meta"][ch]["sensor"] == sensor})
                                        for sig, ch, sensor in (("DA", "redL", "rDAh"), ("Ach", "greenL", "Ach3.0")) for g in ("wt", "ff", "cko")})
# Kernels. Ach: cKO larger than both controls at negative shifts (before side entry), bands not overlapping; read (i) at every
# negative shift, (ii) for the mean over the 20 negative shifts. DA: bands of each pair of genotypes overlap at every shift.
rows = []
for pset in ("P1", "P2"):
    for pool in ("G1", "G2", "G3"):
        for w in ["AA", "Aa", "aA", "aa", "AB", "Ab", "aB", "ab"]:
            K = {(sig, g): kernel(H11[(sig, g, pset)], pool, f"side_entry_{w}") for sig in ("DA", "Ach") for g in ("wt", "ff", "cko")}
            shifts = K[("Ach", "cko")][1]; neg = shifts < 0
            lo = {k: v[0].mean(0) - v[0].std(0) for k, v in K.items()}; hi = {k: v[0].mean(0) + v[0].std(0) for k, v in K.items()}
            above = [(lo[("Ach", "cko")][neg] > hi[("Ach", c)][neg]) for c in ("ff", "wt")]
            m_neg = {g: K[("Ach", g)][0][:, neg].mean(1) for g in ("wt", "ff", "cko")}
            mean_above = all(m_neg["cko"].mean() - m_neg["cko"].std() > m_neg[c].mean() + m_neg[c].std() for c in ("ff", "wt"))
            overlap = [((lo[("DA", a)] <= hi[("DA", b)]) & (lo[("DA", b)] <= hi[("DA", a)])) for a, b in (("cko", "ff"), ("cko", "wt"), ("ff", "wt"))]
            rows.append(dict(predictors=pset, pooling=pool, history=w, ach_neg_shifts_cko_above_both=int((above[0] & above[1]).sum()), of=int(neg.sum()),
                             ach_negmean_cko=m_neg["cko"].mean(), ach_negmean_ff=m_neg["ff"].mean(), ach_negmean_wt=m_neg["wt"].mean(), ach_negmean_cko_above_both=mean_above,
                             da_shifts_all_bands_overlap=int(np.logical_and.reduce(overlap).sum()), da_of=len(shifts)))
k11 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(k11.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print(k11.groupby(["predictors", "pooling"]).agg(ach_all_neg_shifts_all_histories=("ach_neg_shifts_cko_above_both", lambda x: bool((x == 20).all())),
                                                 ach_negmean_all_histories=("ach_negmean_cko_above_both", "all"),
                                                 da_all_shifts_overlap_all_histories=("da_shifts_all_bands_overlap", lambda x: bool((x == 41).all())),
                                                 da_shifts_overlap_fraction=("da_shifts_all_bands_overlap", lambda x: x.sum() / (41 * len(x)))).to_string())

Result: not reproduced. With one model per genotype over all its sessions (G1) and P1, all six R2 are within tolerance (DA 0.136, 0.125 and 0.163, Ach 0.208, 0.269 and 0.221 for WT, Drd2 f/f and Drd2-cKO), and five of six with P2 (DA f/f 0.135, just above 0.134); with one model per mouse or per session every R2 is above its tolerance, so the R2 part depends on the reading. Averaged over the 20 negative shifts, the cKO side-entry Ach kernel lies above both controls with the run bands apart for all eight histories under 5 of 6 readings (under G1 with P2 not for aB); shift by shift it does so at 6 to 20 of the 20 shifts, and under no reading at every shift for all eight histories. The DA kernels' bands of all three genotypes overlap at only 18 to 41% of the history-shift points, so "comparable" fails under every reading; the bands are the s.d. over runs of the same data and are narrow. The kernels of the four rewarded histories are taken with the reward kernel added, as the two are not identified apart. Y = 3 gives the same pattern: under G1 all six R2 are within tolerance with P1 and with P2 (DA f/f 0.134), and under G2 and G3 every R2 is above it. The criterion requires every part under every reading. The R2 part holds under G1 only, the Ach-kernel part holds only for the mean over shifts and there under 5 of 6 readings, and shift by shift under none, and the DA part fails under every reading. No part holds as the criterion states it. The run bands are narrow, so the DA overlap test the claims file names would fail for almost any data. Round 1 recorded partially reproduced; the third verification round agreed with the change to not reproduced.

Blocked claims¶

  • ed7e-cin-activation-evokes-da: the laser artefact shows that the mCherry hemisphere was illuminated in all 7 sessions, and its dLight1.1 trace is not stored (section above).
  • fig3d-telc-abolishes-ach: its 3 mice with Ach3.0 and TelC or mCherry in VLS CINs are not in the dataset. The Fig. 3 sessions the export table lists all carry dLight1.1; the mice it lists for Fig. 3 that the dataset lacks (S731, S734, S803, S804, S998, S999, S1001) may be them. The within-mouse comparison of ed8g is a different design.
  • fig3c-telc-blocks-cin-evoked-da-in-vitro and fig4ef-d2r-needed-for-cin-pause: slice amperometry and cell-attached recordings; the dataset holds no slice data.
  • fig5a-inputs-to-vls: histology; not in the dataset.
  • fig3g-dan-inhibition-lowers-da: no stGtACR2 session is in the dataset (no session has laser onsets outside the CIN-stimulation cohort); the six Fig4 "Chat Dat" mice the export table lists (S1183 to S1241) have no session in it.
  • fig4bc-da-bidirectionally-controls-ach: the head-fixed sessions on the wheel are not in the dataset.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Cohorts come from the export table, not from the paper's data folders, and some differ in size from the paper's (Fig. 1: 14 DA and 16 Ach mice against 13 and 14; jRCaMP1b: 9 against 6; cortical TelC: 3 against 5). The behaviour claims of Extended Data Fig. 1 use the Fig. 1 mice. The LDA uses scikit-learn's shrinkage LDA in place of MATLAB's optimised fitcdiscr. The RFLR is fitted by maximum likelihood with Nelder-Mead in place of the unpublished SGD module. Decision time and ITI are taken from the trials table's entry and exit times. The whole-session cross-correlation uses 54-ms samples in place of 18-ms ones. The GLM code is not published; its pooling and predictor set are run under each reading. Every reading the claims file names is shown. Where a criterion names its readings, the outcome must hold under each; the round-1 outcomes of fig1e-reward-outcome-not-pre and ed8g-vls-telc-ach-suppressed took one reading, and the third verification round agreed to change them, and ed11-cko-glm-r2, to not reproduced. fig1f-cue-omission rests on the paper's script for which sessions omitted the cues.

What was found about the dataset. The files hold no figure, cohort or genotype labels and placeholder subject metadata (age P0D, sex U), so most claims need the export repository's table, which the dataset's metadata links. The trials tables' times are not on the photometry clock (offsets of -125 to +1.2 s), though their sample indices are; their ITI equals centre entry minus the previous side exit from the sample indices. The trials tables' laser columns are False where the laser channel shows stimulation at side entry, and the laser artefact shows that the CIN-stimulation sessions illuminated the right, mCherry, fibre. 193 named channels lack their raw trace and 30 also their z-scored trace, which removes the right-hemisphere dLight1.1 of the CIN-stimulation mice and the raw traces of the thalamic mCherry mice, which carry the cortical controls' retrograde mCherry virus. The stored baseline_f0 is not on the scale of the raw trace. The sensor field holds virus codes in four mice. Nothing marks the cue-omission sessions, and their LED channel has cue onsets in every trial. The cohorts of the VLS-TelC behaviour comparison were run under different reward probabilities and block lengths. The slice, histology, head-fixed and DAN-inhibition data, the dLight1.1 mutant and 21 mice named in the export table are not in the dataset.
